## 9d98a8d91a63

**Reproduced generator-domain omission / plausible color-role shortcut.** Generator SHA-256 `40792864ca96fce0fbd57fa0c6812a643eb8c18057a9949dc7d6eeeef6e3422f`; executed rule hash `8127f612f248`.

The intended rule recolors only color-7 components touching exactly two borders. A stronger shortcut—recolor every nonbackground component touching exactly two borders, regardless of color—fits all 4/4 canonical training pairs: canonical non-7 distractors exist, but none touches exactly two borders. It also fits every current generated input because the generator and validator permit only colors 0 and 7.

The retained 6×6 counterfactual puts a color-4 L on the top-left corner and a color-7 L on the bottom-right corner; each touches exactly two borders. Canonical Racket preserves the color-4 component and recolors only the color-7 component to 6. The rival recolors both, differing on the three color-4 cells. The input is in the broader canonical task domain—canonical demonstrations already establish non-7 distractor objects—but the current `self_check` rejects it with `unexpected non-{0,7} colors in grid: [4]`, so this is specifically a coverage/domain omission rather than a mislabeled generated sample.

With seed 0 and sample indices 0–99 in default/easy/medium/hard, all 400/400 generated inputs passed `self_check` and all 400 used only colors 0 and 7. A repair should add non-7 distractors, including at least one exactly-two-border case per lesson, while retaining color-7 targets and checking the color-agnostic rival executably.

Evidence: `checks/audit/9d98a8d91a63/counterexample.json`, `input.json`, `racket.json`, `rival.json`, `canonical-rival-check.json`, and `sampling.json`. Audit only; target source was not changed.
